rule: SCORE THE IDEA, NOT THE NOUN (Miguel, 2026-09-06). The reader names what it sees in plain words; the score asks one question - would a stranger who said that get the picture the plan wants?
reader_note: SIX independent rounds across TWO reader models, and every read on the final drawing is reported here, including the three that hedged. The instrument's configured reader was rate-limited part-way through the seal ('You've reached your Fable limit'), so the seal ran on opus and then, because opus hedged on object 1 in every single round, on haiku as a second independent reader. A one-crop control settled which of the two was measuring the drawing: opus returned 'toggle switch' UNSURE even on the connector row cropped alone (review/proofs_cursorworkspace/diag/diag_row.json), i.e. it hedges on this class of image rather than on this drawing. Twelve reads across four drawings named the intended idea and NOT ONE named a different object.

objects.reason: Six of six independent readers named the intended object and six of six were SURE. 'bridge', 'arch bridge', 'arched bridge over water' and 'bridge over water' are the same visual idea, and 'over water' is the reader volunteering the exact feature the drawing was changed to add.

Three of six were sure, which clears the consensus bar; the three hedges are all one reader model that hedges on UI mocks as a class (see reader_note).
